title: Refuse unknown top-level arguments before state-changing delegation MCP operations
outcome: Refuse unknown top-level arguments before state-changing delegation MCP operations
acceptance: For exactly these eleven delegation MCP tools—termal_spawn_session, termal_cancel_session, termal_resume_session, termal_followup_session, termal_resume_after_delegations, termal_resume_after_test_runs, termal_send_to_session, termal_read_mailbox, termal_acknowledge_mailbox, termal_board_set, termal_evaluate_acceptance—a request containing a top-level argument outside that tool's accepted argument set is refused with the offending field named before the requested operation performs HTTP I/O or any local mutation. Misspelled optional fields cannot be silently converted into omission/default behavior; the existing caller-eligibility checks remain authoritative.

Each of those tools advertises additionalProperties:false, and its runtime accepted-key check agrees with its input schema. Preserve the mailbox read handler's currently accepted optional readKey by listing it explicitly in that schema and allowlist; retain existing bridge-owned receipt issuance, read-key replay/validation and authority rules. Do not apply argument-name restrictions inside arbitrary user data such as board value, prompts or messages.

Deterministic bridge tests cover unknown top-level keys for all eleven tools and demonstrate zero requested-effect HTTP calls, including misspelled spawn cwd/writePolicy, evaluator reuseDelegationId/criterionEvidence, mailbox afterSequence/receipt/noContinuation, and board value alongside delete:true. Positive controls preserve valid omissions, JSON-null versus absent board values, explicit deletion, numeric versus receipt ACKs, caller restrictions, exact replay keys and mailbox readKey behavior. Existing nested write-policy and submission validation is retained.

Focused validation and the maintained full gate pass on the exact final input, reviewed by fresh independent read-only Codex and Claude whole-input children with no outstanding in-scope Medium or higher. The change does not revise valid default behavior, cancellation/resume authority, HTTP endpoint contracts, source-root naming/clearing/release, queued review-input identity semantics or repository authority instructions. The nine observational/polling tools identified in the inventory remain explicitly outside this fix.
